title: How Much Spatial Control Is Enough? Subdomain Optimal Control of Reaction-Diffusion Systems in Synthetic Developmental Biology
summary: Reaction--diffusion systems can produce spatial patterns such as stripes and spots by diffusion-driven instability. In synthetic developmental biology, such patterns are engineered in cell populations, and steering them toward a prescribed target pattern can be formulated as an optimal control problem. When the control acts on the entire spatial domain, the existence of optimal controls and the first-order optimality conditions are well established.
